clue.text: Red Sea changed colour

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the sea's name are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A remark that the waters of the Red Sea have shifted their hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges REDSEA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reseda is a pale greyish-green shade, named after the mignonette plant.

clue.text: About to join Clara and Al for driving back ?

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Dame Clara Butt was a famous English contralto singer
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to join two friends, Clara and Al, for a drive home.
explanation.walkthrough: Clara Butt (1872-1936) was a celebrated British contralto; her surname supplies the middle. 'driving back' means repelling an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal repels an argument or charge, forcing it back with counter-evidence.

clue.text: One comparatively keen to cheat ?

parts.note: the comparative of an adjective for keen, which is also a noun for a swindler

explanation.surface: Describing someone rather eager to swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both the comparative of 'sharp' (keener) and a noun for a card cheat or swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: More keen-edged is the comparative form; a cardsharp or swindler is also called this.

clue.text: With which to make a fresh impression daily

definitions.text: With which to make a fresh impression daily

parts.words: With which to make a fresh impression daily
parts.note: an office tool reset each day to print the current day's date

explanation.surface: Advice on how to impress people anew every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a fresh impression' suggests winning people over; it means stamping a new print, changed every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A date stamp is an adjustable rubber stamp printing the current date on documents.

clue.text: Immaculate, if not so observant?

explanation.surface: Someone spotless, or perhaps merely someone who notices less.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as SPOT LESS: one who spots less is not so observant.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a blemish means perfectly clean; and one who notices fewer things 'spots less', the question mark flagging the wordplay.

clue.text: The old machines appear to be of very little value

definitions.text: appear to be of very little value

explanation.surface: Antique vehicles that look worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victorian high-wheeled bicycle was named after two small British coins, the penny and the farthing (a quarter of a penny).
explanation.definitionFit: These were early bicycles with a huge front wheel; a penny and a farthing were tiny sums of money.

clue.text: Cast worth re-shaping

indicators.note: re-shaping signals that the letters of worth are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A mould whose value lies in its reworking.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-shaping' rearranges WORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to hurl or fling, as one does a ball.

clue.text: They get taken in by foreigners

definitions.text: They get taken in by foreigners

parts.words: They get taken in by foreigners
parts.note: goods shipped abroad are received by overseas buyers

explanation.surface: People who are duped by visitors from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being deceived; here it means received, as goods sent abroad are taken in by other countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold abroad are bought and received by overseas customers.

clue.text: Like a wedding guest who was also wiser

definitions.text: Like a wedding guest who was also wiser

parts.words: Like a wedding guest who was also wiser
parts.note: Coleridge's Ancient Mariner ends with the Wedding-Guest rising the next morning more sorrowful and more wise

explanation.surface: Describing a wedding guest who had learned something.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's 'Rime of the Ancient Mariner' ends: 'A sadder and a wiser man, He rose the morrow morn.'
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's Wedding-Guest left more sorrowful as well as wiser, the comparative of unhappy.

clue.text: One wouldn't expect to have any truck with this

definitions.text: One wouldn't expect to have any truck with this

parts.words: One wouldn't expect to have any truck with this
parts.note: a rail service for people, not goods, so no freight wagons are attached

explanation.surface: Something a respectable person would avoid having dealings with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have any truck with' means having dealings with; in railway terms a truck is an open goods wagon, absent from a train carrying people.
explanation.definitionFit: A train carrying travellers rather than freight has coaches, not goods trucks.

clue.text: Craft at the end is needed to run this

definitions.text: Craft at the end is needed to run this

parts.words: Craft at the end is needed to run this
parts.note: a train that runs to meet a ship, so a vessel waits at its terminus

explanation.surface: A remark that a ship must be waiting at the finish for this service to operate.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed reads 'tho' for 'the'. 'Craft' suggests skill, but it is a ship: a boat train runs to a port to connect with a sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat train is a rail service timed to connect with a ferry or liner at the coast.

clue.text: Quick — more than one may get shot

definitions.text: more than one may get shot

explanation.surface: A fast gunfight in which several people may be hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Canoeists 'shoot the rapids', riding down a fast stretch of river; one such stretch is a rapid.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick is a synonym of fast; and a stretch of fast, broken river water is one of the rapids that boatmen shoot.

clue.text: Finger-print experts ?

parts.note: people skilled at printing with their fingers on keys, not detectives reading fingerprints

explanation.surface: Forensic specialists who identify fingerprints.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Finger-print' as printing with fingers: those who make letters appear by striking keys.
explanation.definitionFit: These office workers produce printed text by tapping a keyboard with their fingers.

clue.text: We're yet in process of growing

definitions.text: We're yet in process of growing

indicators.note: something still growing is changing shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that they have not finished growing up yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in process of growing' rearranges WEREYET into the answer, and a yew is a tree still growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yew is a slow-growing evergreen conifer, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Arterial highway of vital importance

parts.note: an arterial road suggests traffic, but this is the body's main artery, a route that keeps us alive

explanation.surface: A major trunk road that the nation's transport depends on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arterial highway' sounds like a main road; read literally it is the chief artery, and 'vital' means life-sustaining.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the great artery carrying blood from the heart, essential to life.

clue.text: Well ordered state of the pure in spirit?

definitions.text: Well ordered state of the pure in spirit?

parts.words: Well ordered state of the pure in spirit?
parts.note: tidiness, and also the condition of spirits drunk undiluted, the second reading turning on neat meaning unmixed

explanation.surface: A tidy condition belonging to the spiritually pure, as in the Beatitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pure in spirit' echoes the Beatitudes, but means alcohol taken straight, without water: neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness and order is this quality; spirit drunk undiluted is also called neat.

clue.text: Went short, changing direction

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who ran short of something and changed course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges WENTSHORT.
explanation.definitionFit: This compass point lies between two cardinal points, so it names a bearing.

clue.text: Refined, like three little Wonderland sisters

explanation.surface: Three little sisters from Wonderland with good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Dormouse's tale in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, three sisters, Elsie, Lacie and Tillie, lived at the bottom of a treacle well, so they were raised in a well.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined means having good breeding and manners; the Dormouse's three sisters were brought up at the bottom of a treacle well.

clue.text: Mrs Jorrocks for instance, useful at the start of the hunt

parts.note: being useful is being a help
a hunt begins at the meet, where riders and hounds gather

explanation.surface: Praise for a fox-hunting wife who makes herself handy as the hunt sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed reads 'bunt' for 'hunt'. Mrs Jorrocks is the wife of John Jorrocks, the sporting grocer in R. S. Surtees's comic hunting novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmeet is a wife or helpful partner, and Mrs Jorrocks is a fictional wife.

clue.text: In twelve places king made her cross

definitions.text: In twelve places king made her cross

parts.words: In twelve places king made her cross
parts.note: Edward I set up memorial crosses for his queen at the twelve places where her funeral procession rested

explanation.surface: A king who angered a woman wherever he went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made her cross' suggests angering her; Edward I raised the twelve Eleanor crosses (Charing Cross is one) marking his queen's funeral route to London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward I's queen, Eleanor of Castile, is the woman whose stone crosses stand along her funeral route.

clue.text: Anna and fifteen companions

parts.note: anna was an Indian coin, sixteen of which made up a larger unit

explanation.surface: A girl named Anna out with fifteen friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anna' looks like a woman's name; it is the old Indian coin, sixteen of which made one rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the old Indian currency sixteen annas made one rupee, so one anna plus fifteen more is the whole coin.

clue.text: Yes, pals perhaps, but locked in battle

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of the two words may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Friends agreeing, though they are locked in a fight with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges YESPALS. Plassey (1757) was Clive's victory in Bengal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 gave the East India Company control of Bengal.

clue.text: Some shoe-leather with which to step backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backwards tells us the word for a step is written in reverse order

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A piece of shoe leather used for stepping back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns PACE into ECAP, which follows TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced leather covering the front of a shoe.

clue.text: Take in, in excess of the quota

definitions.text: Take in, in excess of the quota

parts.words: Take in, in excess of the quota
parts.note: to consume food beyond one's proper ration

explanation.surface: Accepting more of something than the allotted quota allows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' suggests accepting or deceiving; here it means eating, and doing so beyond the allowance is gluttony.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to consume more food than one needs.

clue.text: Where, in Eire, Thackeray finished one of his novels ?

indicators.note: finished points to the ending of the novel title, dropping its opening letters

parts.note: Pendennis is a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray

explanation.surface: Asking where in Ireland Thackeray completed one of his books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished' keeps only the end of Thackeray's 'Pendennis'. Ennis is the county town of Clare in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennis is a town in County Clare in the Irish Republic, so it is a place in Eire.

clue.text: The last man to join a Friendly Society ?

definitions.text: The last man to join a Friendly Society ?

parts.words: The last man to join a Friendly Society ?
parts.note: the biblical outcast whose hand was against every man would be least likely to join any friendly club

explanation.surface: Naming the newest member to sign up with a mutual-aid association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last man to join' looks like the latest recruit; it means the least likely. Genesis says of Ishmael 'his hand will be against every man'. A Friendly Society is a British mutual insurance club.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's son in Genesis became the archetype of the outcast, hostile to everyone, so the least sociable of men.

clue.text: One cleric who is able to get on

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A clergyman capable of getting ahead in his career.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a clergyman serving on the chapter of a cathedral.

clue.text: He's the first to give offence

definitions.text: He's the first to give offence

parts.words: He's the first to give offence
parts.note: the one who strikes first, starting a fight or war

explanation.surface: A remark about the person who is always quickest to cause insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give offence' suggests insulting someone; it means launching an attack (an offensive).
explanation.definitionFit: The party who attacks without provocation is the one starting hostilities.

clue.text: But it should be rendered in its entirety

definitions.text: But it should be rendered in its entirety

parts.words: But it should be rendered in its entirety
parts.note: a paradox: a piece whose name says it is only a fraction, yet must be performed whole

explanation.surface: An objection that something should be performed complete, not in pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The name says 'part', yet a choral piece for several voices is sung right through; 'rendered' means performed.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song is a choral composition for several voices, each singing its own line.

clue.text: Remained sober, by the, sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells us the word meaning sober is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: staid means sober and sedate

explanation.surface: Someone who kept off the drink, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: STAID and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed is a past tense meaning kept to one place, waited on.
